author: Tracy Withers
description: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon called a Nov. 7 national election, aiming to win a second term in government with a promise of delivering faster economic growth.
title: NZ Election Set for Nov. 7 as Luxon Seeks Second Term

author: Maya Davis
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called for dismantling the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, revitalizing the “Abolish ICE” rhetoric that became popular in progressive discourse during the last Trump administration as pushback against the latest deportation efforts intensifies.
title: ‘Abolish ICE’ Calls Get Louder With NYC’s Mamdani Joining Chorus

author: Ella Feldman
description: US military forces seized a seventh tanker near Venezuela Tuesday as the Trump administration continues to pressure the South American country to halt its use of sanctioned ships and clamps down on the nation’s oil trade.
title: US Captures Seventh Sanctioned Oil Tanker Linked to Venezuela

description: Meredith Crowley, University of Cambridge Professor of Economics, discusses the potential economic impacts President Trump's Greenland tariff threats could have on Europe & what restrictions and retaliation plans Europe has suggested if the President acts on his threats. She speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How Might Europe Respond to Trump's Greenland Tariff Threats?

author: Greg Stohr, Erik Larson
description: Months after President Donald Trump attempted to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over unproven mortgage fraud allegations, the case will get a hearing before the Supreme Court.
title: Can Trump Fire Lisa Cook? What the Supreme Court Will Consider

description: ICE has been open about its aggressive detention and deportation targets. Now, the agency has its sights set on a new kind of facility to house the people it arrests: converted warehouses. Bloomberg reporters Fola Akinnibi and Sophie Alexander walk host Sarah Holder through how that expansion could play out on the Big Take podcast (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Deadly Risks of ICE’s Rapid Expansion Plans

description: BondBloxx Co-Founder Joanna Gallegos joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the state of corporate credit as 2026 begins amid a flurry of geopolitical activity. Gallegos says the thru-line of corporate credit strength is still in place for the year. She also discusses where along the curve investors are flocking, corporate debt, and more. Gallegos speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Corporate Credit 'Resilient' Heading Into 2026: BondBloxx's Gallegos

description: Leon Panetta, former Secretary of Defense, reacts to President Trump voicing his need to acquire Greenland and states the President's continued threats will hurt the US economy and create an affordability problem. Panetta also insists that the President needs to negotiate with Greenland and shares his reaction to Trump's proposed "Board of Peace." He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Does Trump Want to Hurt US Economy or Negotiate: Panetta

description: Bob Michele, Chief Investment Officer and Head of GFICC at JPMorgan Asset Management, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the global bond market selloff as geopolitical concerns shake up what has been a calm start to the year so far. Michele also says he believes Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is now the likeliest candidate to become Federal Reserve chairman. Michele speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: JPM's Michele Sees Treasury Secretary Bessent as Fed Frontrunner

author: Alessandra Migliaccio, Ania Nussbaum, Irina Vilcu, Ben Sills
description: The European Union faces a stress test of whether it can respond as a united force when its sovereignty is challenged.
title: Trump’s Greenland Threat Is Stirring Up Europe’s Deepest Divisions

author: Naomi Ng, Eleanor Harrison-Dengate, K Oanh Ha
description: Trillions of dollars in Japanese assets are held by people at risk of cognitive decline. On today’s Big Take Asia podcast, what this “dementia money cliff” means for the nation and the broader global economy.
title: Japan's ‘Dementia Money’ Crisis Puts Trillions of Dollars at Risk

description: President Donald Trump said that federal immigration agents sometimes make mistakes, even as he broadly defended his migrant crackdown. He spoke at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: ICE Agents Makes 'Mistakes' Sometimes, President Trump Says

description: President Donald Trump doubles down on his efforts to take control of Greenland before heading to Davos. “I think that we will work something out where NATO is going to be very happy and where we’re going to be very happy,” Trump said. “But we need it for security purposes. We need it for national security and even world security. It’s very important.” He spoke at the White House press briefing.  (Source: Bloomberg)

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: European nations weigh how to respond to Trump’s latest tariff threats.
title: Trump’s Greenland Quest Has Allies Reeling — and Pushing Back

description: President Trump touted achievements from the first year of his second term in office and answered questions from reporters at the White House press briefing. The president said that he believes NATO will be very happy with the outcome of his push for US control of Greenland and said that he doubts the tension over the threats will have any impact on trade agreements with EU nations. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He Doubts Greenland Tariff Threats Will Impact EU Trade Deals: Q&A

author: Chris Strohm, Miranda Davis
description: The Justice Department sent grand jury subpoenas to multiple top Minnesota officials in a widening investigation over whether they conspired to impede federal immigration enforcement efforts, according to a person familiar with the matter.
title: DOJ Subpoenas Pressure Top Minnesota Officials Over Immigration

description: "I’m a big fan of the UN potential, but it has never lived up to its potential,” President Donald Trump tells reporters at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Suggests Board of Peace Might Replace UN

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: Vice President JD Vance and his wife Usha Vance are expecting their fourth child, a boy, the couple announced.
title: Vance, Wife Usha Expecting Fourth Child, Couple Announces

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bob Michele of JPMorgan Asset Management about the bond market's global selloff as concerns about Greenland and Japan dominate the opening of the World Economic Forum. Then, Bloomberg's Julie Fine recaps her interview with Former Dallas Fed President Robert Kaplan as he weighs in on the next potential Fed Chair. Plus, Bloomberg's Mike McKee joins to discuss why that Fed Chair search is turning into a hunt for an elusive unicorn. Finally, Joanna Gallegos of BondBloxx weighs in on the state of corporate credit. (Source: Bloomberg)

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump expressed confidence that the European Union would continue to invest in the US even if he imposed new tariffs related to his quest to take control of Greenland, a proposal that has angered leaders on the continent.
title: Trump Doubts Greenland Threats Will Spoil Trade Deal With Europe

author: Alex Vasquez, Gonzalo Soto
description: Mexico handed over a new group of inmates with alleged ties to drug cartels to US authorities, the latest sign of changes in security cooperation with Washington under President Claudia Sheinbaum.
title: Mexico Sends Third Group of Inmates With Cartel Ties to US

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: Congressional lawmakers green-lighting $839 billion in US defense spending voiced strong support for an embattled test office at the Pentagon that was slashed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, highlighting its value at preventing the “catastrophic failure” of US weapons and military equipment.

author: Larry Arnold
description: How could a sitting US president be legally removed from office? Most people have heard of impeachment, a power granted to (and rarely used by) the US Congress. But there’s also the 25th amendment to the US Constitution, which provides an avenue for a president to be removed under extraordinary circumstances by his or her own leadership team. A handful of Democratic lawmakers have advocated the amendment’s use to unseat President Donald Trump over what they consider his erratic behavior regardin
title: Could the Constitution’s 25th Amendment Be Used to Oust Trump?

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump suggested his proposed Board of Peace could supplant an ineffective United Nations, while asserting that the decades-old outfit still could assist in his peacekeeping efforts.
title: Trump Suggests Board of Peace Could Supplant United Nations

author: Leah Nylen, Josh Sisco
description: The US Federal Trade Commission will appeal a federal judge’s decision that Meta Platforms Inc. doesn’t have a monopoly in social networking, an agency spokesman said Tuesday.
title: US FTC to Appeal Court Ruling on Meta Win in Monopoly Case

description: European leaders should follow Sun Tzu’s advice in Greenland: Never pick a fight you can’t win, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Marc Champion says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Greenland Isn’t a Fight Europe Can Win

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu discusses President Trump's latest comments about Greenland. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Takes Affordability Pitch to Davos | Balance of Power: Early Edition 1/20/2026

description: Former State Department official Daniel Fried said it's unclear whether Trump's threats to seize Greenland are real or a negotiating ploy but there still is a path to an outcome that gives the US more of presence on the Arctic island and keeps the NATO alliance intact. Fried also weighed in on the presidents offer of a seat on his newly announced 'board of peace' to Russian president Vladimir Putin, saying he doesn't understand the 'sense' of the offer for US interests.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Almost 'No Case' For Trump's Greenland's Demands, Says Daniel Fried

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump said that federal immigration agents sometimes make mistakes, even as he broadly defended his migrant crackdown that has sparked tensions in cities nationwide.
title: Trump Says ICE Makes ‘Mistakes’ While Backlash to Tactics Grows

author: Laura Nahmias, Danielle Muoio Dunn, Raga Justin
description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul isn’t raising income or corporate taxes this year to fund the state’s $260 billion budget, easing concerns from some business leaders after Zohran Mamdani was elected mayor in a campaign that promised hikes on the city’s richest residents and businesses.

description: Ukraine’s military is working to replace Chinese-made drones with domestically produced models to cut the war-ravaged nation’s dependence on imports and sanctioned supply lines, the newly appointed defense minister said.
title: Ukraine’s New Defense Minister Pushes for More Domestic Drones

author: Josh Wingrove
description: The powers he’s assumed in his second term will surely outlast him. Democrats could be counting on it.

description: Russia poses a clear threat in the Arctic, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told world leaders in Davos, Switzerland, though at this stage it is “more prospective than actual.”

description: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce discusses the regulation of the crypto industry and expanding the trading hours of tokenized stocks on "Bloomberg Crypto." (Source: Bloomberg)

description:
Henrietta Treyz, Managing Partner and Director of Economic Policy at Veda Partners, to Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss EU reciprocal tariffs, Greenland the looming US Government Shutdown.  

 Lawmakers clinched a deal on their last set of spending bills as Congress races to fund the government by the Jan. 30 deadline.

 US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged calm amid a growing transatlantic rift over President Donald Trump’s ambitions to take over Greenland, calling for allies to honor their trade agreements and dismissing suggestions that Europe would forcefully retaliate by dumping US treasuries. (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Canada stands with Greenland and Denmark and their right to determine Greenland's future, says Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in an address at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland.  (Source: Bloomberg)

author: Josh Wingrove, Saleha Mohsin, Joshua Green
description: President Donald Trump’s search for a new Federal Reserve chair is becoming a hunt for an elusive unicorn candidate as blowback from his attacks on the central bank complicates the decision.
title: Trump’s Fed Chair Search Is Becoming Hunt for Elusive Unicorn

author: Kamlesh Bhuckory, Joe Mayes
description: More than two centuries of British control over the Chagos Islands are coming to an end after the government agreed to cede ownership of the Indian Ocean archipelago to Mauritius and pay an annual fee to allow the UK and US to maintain a key military base there.

description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics is poised to get a slight funding boost this year and stay housed within the Labor Department, according to a bipartisan budget deal that’s expected to pass this month.

description: Tariffs, tax cuts, deregulation – Trump’s first year back has been busy. What’s had the biggest impact and what will stick? Hear David Gura, Nancy Cook and Mark Niquette discuss on the Big Take podcast. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump’s World-Changing Economic Agenda, One Year Later

description: Rachel Reeves said the UK government has done enough on tax and shouldn’t need to come back for more hikes, remarks that risk making her a hostage to fortune.

description: It's been one year since President Trump took the oath of office and Wall Street has responded. Norah Mulinda explains (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Greenland’s prime minister said the Arctic island’s population and its authorities need to start preparing for a possible military invasion, even as it remains an unlikely scenario, as President Donald Trump continues to threaten taking over the territory.

description: Canada stands completely behind Greenland and Denmark, and the world’s middle powers must work together to resist coercion from aggressive superpowers, according to Prime Minister Mark Carney.

description: The US Supreme Court didn’t rule on President Donald Trump’s tariffs Tuesday, meaning it probably will be at least another month before a challenge to his signature economic policy is resolved.

description: Anne Walsh of Guggenheim Partners does not expect to see a recession in the US this year. She says tailwinds for markets are very strong right now, but they could always evaporate. She speaks to Lisa Abramowicz in Davos. (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Along the illustrious Davos Promenade, the US administration has taken over a 19th century church that’s been reconsecrated for the week as a shrine to business and politics. On the eve of President Donald Trump’s arrival, a banner hangs behind USA House spelling out, “House of God.”

description: Finnish President Alexander Stubb discusses current geopolitical tensions regarding Greenland and US President Donald Trump’s interest in the island. Stubb speaks on Bloomberg Television at the World Economic Forum’s annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland.

Macron Says US Tariffs Used as Leverage 'Unacceptable' (Video)

title: Russian Oil Exports Plunge to 4-Month Low as India Shuns Cargoes

Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Canada, discusses how diplomacy drives trade, how Canada balances economic engagement with global leadership, its push to expand trade beyond the United States, and why it continues to stand four-square behind its NATO allies, in conversation with Bloomberg’s Lisa Abramowicz at Bloomberg House in Davos on the sidelines of the 2026 World Economic Forum. description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia.

On today's show, US President Trump posts a screenshot of a message on Truth Social that was written by French President Emmanuel Macron. In the screenshot, Macron says he does not understand what Trump is doing on Greenland.

Bloomberg understands that Macron doesn’t plan to join Trump’s proposed Gaza Board of Peace. Bloomberg understands the US President wants the full constitution and remit of the committee signed in Davos on Thursday.

US equity futures slid more than 1% and European contracts edged lower as Trump’s tariff threats over Greenland revived trade tensions.

Today's guests: State Street CEO Ron O'Hanley, Egypt Investment & Trade Minister, Hassan El-Khatib & Bradshaw Advisory Senior Adviser, Crawford Falconer (Source: Bloomberg)

description:
The yen is falling and it's partly due to political uncertainty after Japan's PM Sanae Takaichi called for a snap election to take place on Feb. 8.

But bad news for the yen could mean good news for the stock market. Ruth Carson explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Japan's Snap Election Means for the Yen

description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi lacks a silver bullet to fund a sales tax cut without stoking concerns that she is moving toward the fiscal direction of former UK leader Liz Truss.
title: Takaichi’s Tax Cut Plan Stokes Fiscal Fears With Unclear Funding

author: Yoshiaki Nohara
description: Japan is preparing for a snap lower-house election that could reshape the country’s political balance at a moment of economic strain and regional uncertainty.
title: Why a Snap Election Is a Gamble for Japan’s Prime Minister

author: Hallie Gu, Alfred Cang
description: China has purchased roughly 12 million tons of US soybeans in the last three months, clearing a closely watched trade hurdle and meeting a key pledge outlined by the Trump administration in November.
title: China Reaches 12 Million Tons of Soy Purchases to Meet US Pledge

author: Niki Koswanage, Tom Redmond
description: The family of Altantuya Shaariibuu, who was murdered in 2006 by two bodyguards assigned to protect officials including former Malaysian premier Najib Razak, lost their bid for damages from the Malaysian government after a court upheld its appeal.
title: Malaysia Wins Appeal in Lawsuit by Murdered Mongolian’s Family

author: Zoe Tillman
description: The Trump administration urged a judge to reject Minnesota’s request for an immediate order halting the recent escalation of federal immigration enforcement in the state, accusing local authorities of wrongly trying to exercise a “veto” over the US government.
title: Trump Administration Fights in Court to Keep Minnesota ICE Surge

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: Former Thai leader Abhisit Vejjajiva expects to play a kingmaker’s role in any coalition that seeks to rule the Southeast Asian nation after next month’s election, pitching an agenda of “clean politics” to tackle systemic corruption and dismantle cyber scam operations.
title: Thai Ex-Premier Abhisit Seeks Return as Anti-Scammer Kingmaker

author: Joe Mayes
description: The UK government outlined plans to intensify efforts to attract global talent in sectors such as artificial intelligence, life sciences and clean energy, as Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves heads to the World Economic Forum in Davos urging executives to invest in Britain.
title: UK Seeks to Ease Global Talent Visas as Reeves Heads to Davos
